title: Adaptive intake and prioritization matrix for enterprise escalations
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Major customers often surface escalation requests that mix urgent outages, long-term product asks, and strategic commercial asks. Current intake funnels these to a single triage queue with limited signal fusion (contract value, renewal timing, product fit, severity), which leads to inconsistent prioritization and missed SLA expectations for high-value accounts.

Goal: Define and deliver an adaptive admission and prioritization matrix that ranks incoming enterprise escalations by a transparent score combining urgency, revenue/risk, product fit, and implementation cost. The matrix should be operational in the intake spreadsheet, integrated into the account intake form, and surfaced to the roadmap review board as a canonical signal for sprint commitments and canary rollouts.

Why now: Several strategic customers have escalations ahead of renewal and we lack a repeatable rule set to guarantee SLA-backed commitments without starving platform engineering. This is an OKR-linked initiative (OKR: Reduce enterprise escalation-to-commit time to <= 10 business days).
background: We currently route top-account requests through AE/CS intake and a rotating PM triage call. Decisions are ad-hoc and depend on who is on duty. Engineering sees high variance in perceived priority and frequently needs clear acceptance criteria before committing. Past incidents: Q4 2025 had two missed commitments that required discount credits and manual engineering prioritization. Reference: Confluence /docs/top-accounts/incidents/Q4-2025-postmortem and dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/escalation-slo
proposal_steps: Design a scoring rubric with weighted signals: severity (1-5), renewal horizon (days), ARR impact bucket, strategic alignment (yes/no), implementation delta (T-shirt sizing), and dependency complexity.
Implement an intake form change (CS->PM) that populates signals and computes a provisional score; store submissions in shared sheet + automations.
Create a small rules engine in the Console that maps score bands to intake lanes: Immediate SLA (48h commit), High (10 business days), Consider (cycle planning), Decline/Outsource.
Link to backlog gating: high-lane items create a 'fastlane' ticket template with required acceptance criteria and a dedicated exploit/rollback policy.
Run a 6-week pilot with 6 strategic accounts; collect outcome metrics and iterate weights; prepare rollout with 1:1 trainings for CSMs and AEs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form computes score from all required fields and refuses submission if required signals missing.
Rules engine surfaces lane assignment in Console and generates the correct ticket template for 'Immediate' and 'High' lanes.
Pilot with at least 6 accounts completed and we have measurement for time-to-decision and engineering lead time.
Stakeholders (PM, ENG, CS, Legal) sign off on lane definitions and commitment windows.
Operational runbook published in Confluence and onboarding materials for CSMs delivered.
metrics: Primary: Median escalation-to-commit time (business days) — target <= 10 for High, <= 2 for Immediate.
Secondary: Percent of high-score requests honored within SLA (target 90%).
Tertiary: Change in churn risk for participating accounts over 90 days.
Operational: False-positive rate of Immediate lane (requests that were low-effort but marked Immediate).
Business: ARR preserved/accelerated by prioritized deliveries.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize rubric and intake form changes; docs + CS training slides prepared.
Week 3-8: Pilot (6 accounts) with daily standups and one clear escalation contact per account; collect feedback and adjust weights.
Week 9: Retrospective, finalize engine mapping and push small Console feature to show lane tags on tickets.
Week 10-12: Gradual roll out across all AE-managed enterprise accounts and include in roadmap planning ritual; measure OKR metrics weekly.
Post-rollout: Quarterly review to recalibrate weights and expand to Dedicated/Private deployment escalations if successful.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting weights to pilot accounts leading to unfair gating — Mitigation: Use holdout accounts and conservative weight updates.
Risk: Engineering bandwidth spikes for Immediate lane — Mitigation: Define clear rollback/fallback policy and require acceptance criteria up-front.
Risk: CS adoption friction — Mitigation: Provide onboarding, a single-button 'escalate' flow, and weekly office hours for first 6 weeks.
Risk: Legal constraints for certain enterprise asks — Mitigation: Add Legal review step into rules engine for flagged categories.
